To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) canopy management of shaded winegrape vineyards is essential to achieve high yields and good quality; 2) the canopy ideotype provides a framework to achieve this; and 3) point quadrat analysis is a cheap and effective method of assessing canopies.

canopy management is important for improving grape yield and wine quality and that the principles of canopy management should include: (a) the amount of surface area, (b) spacing between canopies, (c) within canopy shade, (d) balance between fruit and leaf growth, and (e) uniformity of location and distribution of fruit/renewals, shoot tips and bud bases.
canopy management can increase grape yield and wine quality, but the effects depend on the canopy structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of canopy structure and microclimate on grape yield and wine quality, and the use of canopy management as a means of improving grape yield and wine quaity.
developing canopy ideotype for winegrapes.
the development of canopy management principles, which are based on a better understanding of the relationship between canopy microclimate and grape yield and wine quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best canopies for yield and wine quality are open and well-lit, and that canopy management techniques should aim to achieve these conditions.
the best canopies for winegrapes have a large amount of surface area with a low leaf area index and high light interception, with uniform fruiting zones, and shoot tips and cane base positions.

the best canopies are those with the highest surface area, with fruit and renewal zones well distributed throughout the canopy, and with a uniform distribution of shade in all parts of the canopy, and particularly within the fruiting zone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the canopy ideotype is the best way of describing and managing a canopy, and that the best canopy is a canopy that is well balanced in its growth and distribution of shoots, buds, and fruit.
the canopy should be divided into two tiers, with the upper tier being a light shade, and the lower tier being exposed to the full sun.

the best canopies for winegrape production are those which have a large surface area with a high percentage of fruit exposed to the light, and which provide a high percentage of the light intercepted by the canopy to be absorbed by the canopy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
canopy division is a simple and cost effective method to increase vineyard yield and quality.
canopy management can increase yield and quality simultaneously.

the best canopy management practices for grape yield and wine quality are to: 1) reduce the amount of fruiting zone leaf area; 2) reduce leaf density and canopy volume; 3) increase the amount of fruit exposed to direct sunlight; 4) increase the amount and intensity of sunlight on the fruiting zone; 5) improve the uniformity of canopy microclimate; and 6) increase the uniformity in location of fruiting/renewal zones.
